subject: FastCart onboarding: throughput targets & acceptance test handoff
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fastcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: FastCart onboarding: throughput targets & acceptance test handoff

Alice —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I sketched a lightweight acceptance plan so your SREs can validate the latency/throughput SLOs before we flip production traffic. High level:

- Target p95 latency: <= 220ms for single-request inference (payload ~256 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s per GPU under mixed prompt sizes (10–512 tokens)
- Burst capability: 400 req/s for 10s window (fallback to queued requests after)

Next steps I propose:
1) Your ops shares a small representative traffic sample or QPS profile.
2) We run a 2-hour acceptance load test in our dedicated staging cluster.
3) We share a CSV of per-request latencies + a summary PDF and a recommended config (batching/kv-cache).

Can you confirm the targets above look reasonable for FastCart? If ok, loop in whoever owns the test harness and we’ll hand off load scripts.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FastCart onboarding: throughput targets & acceptance test handoff

Rishi —

Thanks, that looks aligned with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications:

- Our primary concern is p95 for cart-compute (most requests ~180 tokens). 220ms p95 is acceptable as a starting point.
- Sustained throughput target should reflect expected peak: currently 100–130 req/s per region; we prefer the plan use 120 req/s as you suggested.
- For burst, we need at least 300 req/s for 20s; can you support extending the burst window to 20s?

I’m looping Ben (SRE) and ops for the harness and sample traffic. Ben, can you share a sanitized traffic sample and any CI constraints (IP allowlist, windows, how you prefer CSV vs. JSON logs)?

—Alice

Team —

We completed the acceptance run this morning against the dedicated staging pool. Summary highlights attached (redwood-bench-report-fastcart-20260216.pdf) and raw CSV (fastcart-benchmark-results-20260215.csv). Quick top-line:

- p95 latency (180-token median payload): 208ms
- Sustained 120 req/s per GPU: stable with 8–12% CPU headroom; batching at 64ms window used
- 20s burst to 300 req/s: minor queueing spikes; average p95 during burst 260ms, tail up to 420ms for requests >400 tokens

Recommendations:
- Apply KV prefix caching for repeat cart-summary prompts (we measured a 22% token compute reduction)
- Set burst cap to 300 req/s and enable graceful queuing beyond that threshold with a 10s priority window for checkout requests
- Small model quantization (int8) is optional — reduces cost but raises tail latency for large prompts; recommend A/B test first.

Next steps:
- Monica/CS: propose a 30m review for Tue Feb 17 10:00 PST to walk the PDF and map action items.
- Ops: Redwood will push the CSV and PDF to s3://fastcart-onboarding/results/uploaded-20260216/ and provide a short README.

Thanks everyone — let me know if you want us to tighten p95 further before GA.

—Rishi

Attachments: redwood-bench-report-fastcart-20260216.pdf, fastcart-benchmark-results-20260215.csv
